messages.content: You are the fine-tuned operations agent for a restaurant startup planning app. Use the uploaded operations data pack and stay operationally concrete, beginner-friendly, and realistic. Return strict JSON only.

Founder location: Champaign Campustown near Green Street and student apartments

Budget band: 75k_200k

Cuisine hint: healthy bowls and soup

Business goals: low risk first business with repeat lunch demand and easy operations

Selected concept: Neighborhood small-plates & wine bar

Selected concept opening hours: Tue–Sun 4pm–11pm (kitchen closes ~10:30pm); closed Monday for prep

Knowledge pack:
Operations data pack version: 2026-04-08.
Uploaded source files: ChampaignFoodSanitation.pdf; ChampaignPersonnelPolicy.pdf; Food Preparation and Serving Occupations (BLS OOH).pdf; How to Improve the Restaurant Kitchen Workflow (GloriaFood POS).pdf; How to Optimize a Restaurant Workflow in Less Than a Week.pdf; ISO9001_Quality management systems.pdf; NSF Food Equipment Standards (NSF).pdf; starting-your-business-handbook-2026.pdf.
Inspection cadence baseline: Cat1 at least 3 times/year (one can be approved educational contact); Cat2 at least 1 time/year; Cat3 at least once every 2 years.
Personnel policy signals: full-time minimum 30 hours, part-time maximum 30 hours.
Labor market context: all food prep/serving 34130, cooks 35760, bartenders 33530, waitstaff 33760.
Workflow principles: separate prep/cook/plating/cleaning zones | use FIFO and date labels consistently | keep meat and produce workflows segregated | reduce handoff ambiguity between FOH and BOH.
Core metrics: ticket time by station and daypart | table turn time / order cycle time | orders per labor hour | waste by reason code.
Fast-week roadmap: Day 1: map bottlenecks and observe station handoffs | Day 2: simplify menu and remove low-velocity complexity | Day 3: standardize station SOP checklists | Day 4: run focused cross-training and pre-shift huddles | Day 5: tune POS/KDS/printer routing and 86 alerts | Day 6: run service simulation and collect error logs | Day 7: review KPIs and lock next-week corrective actions.
Equipment standards: NSF/ANSI 2 Food Equipment (general sanitation/design baseline) | NSF/ANSI 3 Commercial Warewashing Equipment | NSF/ANSI 4 Commercial Cooking and Hot Holding | NSF/ANSI 7 Commercial Refrigerators and Freezers | NSF/ANSI 8 Commercial Powered Food Prep Equipment | NSF/ANSI 51 Food Equipment Materials.
Quality system hints: Use process approach and PDCA cycle for operations tuning | Document SOPs and version control for critical procedures | Track nonconformities and corrective actions with owners/dates.

Entry labor market context: cooks median ~$35,760/yr (BLS)."},{"role":"Front-of-house","headcountAtOpen":"2–4","hiringNotes":"Start with a strong trainer shift and written service steps. FOH labor context: waitstaff median ~$33,760/yr."}],"supplierCategories":[{"category":"Broadline distributor or local wholesalers","sourcingTips":"Compare minimums, delivery windows, and credit terms; do not optimize only for price. Add a backup vendor for top-20 SKUs."},{"category":"Produce & specialty","sourcingTips":"Keep backup vendor list for volatile items and apply FIFO + date labeling to reduce spoilage."},{"category":"Packaging & disposables","sourcingTips":"Match packaging to real order mix (dine-in vs. takeout) and track waste reason codes weekly."}],"equipmentHighlights":[{"area":"Cold holding","starterItems":"Reach-in fridge/freezer sized for pars; thermometers + labeling discipline. Prefer equipment aligned with NSF/ANSI 7 Commercial Refrigerators and Freezers and NSF/ANSI 51 Food Equipment Materials."},{"area":"Cook line","starterItems":"Prioritize minimum set that can execute top sellers at peak. Validate line against NSF/ANSI 4 Commercial Cooking and Hot Holding."},{"area":"Dish / three-compartment sink compliance","starterItems":"Confirm health authority layout expectations before buying used equipment.
